newsitem.title: USA: Windmere-Durable says to sign Kmart deal.
newsitem.headline: Windmere-Durable says to sign Kmart deal.

text.p: Windmere-Durable Holdings Inc said on Thursday it is in the "final documentation phase" of a seven-year $1.7 billion agreement to supply Kmart Corp with small appliances and consumer products.

The deal would make Windmere-Durable and two other companies it partially owns, Salton/Maxim Housewares Inc and NewM-Tech, the exclusive mass merchandisers for White-Westinghouse brand appliances in the United States.
The company said it owns 50 percent of both Salton/Maxim and NewM-Tech Corp.
David Friedson, chairman and chief executive of Windmere-Durable, said the company expected to sign a final agreement "within the next couple of days."

Friedson said the deal provides for a minimum purchase of $1.4 billion over the seven-year span, or it could be extended for an additional nine years and $2.5 billion worth of purchases, making the deal worth a potential $4.2 billion.

Items the company would sell to Kmart include small kitchen appliances, fans, heaters and humidifiers from Salton/Maxim and electronic goods such as televisions, audio equipment, telephones, and answering machines from NewM-Tech.
Salton/Maxim and NewM-Tech have licensing and trademark rights for White-Westinghouse's WCI, a unit of Frigidaire Corp.
Friedson said about 40 percent of the sales volume would come through Salton/Maxim and about 60 percent would flow through NewM-Tech.
He added the company wouldn't be supplying Kmart in a significant way until the second half of 1997.
